LipReading.title: Visual Speech Recognition Bengali Language (DL)
LipReading.overview: Bridged the low-resource gap in Bengali visual speech recognition by building LipBengal, the first large-scale Bengali lip-reading dataset, and a 3D CNN + BiLSTM + CTC pipeline to validate it.
methodology: Collected and pre-processed 1400+ hours of video across 150 Bengali speakers into a 500-word annotated lip-reading dataset.
Built a 3D CNN + BiLSTM + CTC pipeline for spatiotemporal feature extraction and sequence modeling, trained in TensorFlow 2.10 on a CUDA-enabled GPU.
Benchmarked dataset quality against LipNet-based baseline experiments.
findings: Achieved 84.6% recognition accuracy on the held-out test set.
Published as first-author work in Data in Brief (Elsevier, Vol 58, 2025).

Tomato Classifier.title: Tomato Ripeness Classification (CNN)
Tomato Classifier.overview: Deep-learning image classifier that distinguishes ripe from unripe tomatoes in real time, benchmarking a custom CNN against transfer-learning baselines.
methodology: Trained and compared three architectures (a custom 'tomato_model' CNN, VGG16, and ResNet50) on a labeled ripe/unripe tomato image set.
Built a train/test split pipeline with checkpointed model weights for reproducible evaluation.
Wired up real-time inference over an IP-Webcam video feed for live classification testing.
findings: The lightweight custom CNN stayed competitive with the deeper transfer-learning baselines while running fast enough for real-time inference.
Pretrained weights are saved for drop-in reuse without retraining.

E-Grenade.title: eGrenade: Electronic 3D Position-Tracking Practice Grenade
E-Grenade.overview: Ongoing research project: a 3D-printed, non-explosive ESP32 practice grenade that senses its own throw and reconstructs a full 3D trajectory onboard, for objective grenade-throwing assessment without external cameras, radar, or motion-capture rigs.
methodology: An ESP32 DevKit V1 runs interrupt-driven acquisition from a GY-87 board (MPU6050 IMU with onboard DMP orientation/gravity output, QMC5883L magnetometer, BMP180 barometer) over I2C, timestamped to the millisecond off the IMU's data-ready pin.

Event detection runs independently of the IMU stream: a Hall-effect sensor and magnet in the detachable safety-lever assembly mark 'activation' the moment the pin/spoon is pulled, while 4 piezoelectric sensors distributed around the body flag ground impact from any landing orientation, driving an Idle to Active to Released to In-flight to Landed to Recovered state machine.

The 3D-printed ABS enclosure is modeled on a BD-84 reference grenade's dimensional envelope (110.64 x 62.76 mm), with a gyroid-infill and TPU-damped internal mount protecting the electronics payload from repeated throw and impact shock, inside a detachable, non-explosive safety-lever assembly that reproduces the real pin-and-spoon interaction.

The ESP32 streams IMU, compass, and barometer data over WiFi UDP using a custom framed binary protocol (magic header, type ID, length, CRC32) to a Python 'digital twin' app, which fuses it through EMA/median/Hampel outlier filtering, an EKF for orientation with compass-yaw correction, zero-velocity updates (ZUPT) and drag compensation to fight position drift, and barometric altitude fusion, plotted live in a 3D path viewer.
findings: Functional prototype assembled at 432 g, about 10% lighter than the 480 g reference grenade, with internal mass kept close to the body centerline to preserve realistic throwing feel and balance.

Live WiFi telemetry and an EKF/ZUPT-based orientation-and-position pipeline are working and tunable end to end; validating trajectory accuracy against ArUco/ChArUco camera ground truth and training an impact/fall classifier are the next steps.

IG ECU.title: Ignition System for Engine Control Unit_STM32
IG ECU.overview: Real-time ignition control unit for STM32F4, built at Creative Factory Labs for a German automotive client, calculating engine RPM from encoder feedback and dynamically timing coil dwell for precise spark control.
methodology: Interrupt-driven design: TIM input-capture for pulse intervals, an EXTI callback for the index/TDC pulse, and timer-based RPM sampling every 50 ms.
Modular IS_Config / IS_State structs abstract hardware wiring from runtime state, with dwell time computed dynamically from live RPM.
UART debug shell streams RPM, dwell pulses, and timing accuracy for live calibration.
findings: Stable ignition timing with accurate spark delivery across a wide RPM range.
Slight timing drift only at low supply voltage and very high engine speed.

7DOF Robotic ARM.title: Object Classification by a 7-DOF Robotic Arm Using MobileNet-SSD and Feedback Position Mapping
7DOF Robotic ARM.overview: A 7-DOF MG996R/ATmega2560 robotic arm that classifies and sorts cups vs. bottles using MobileNet-SSDV3, controlled through feedback position mapping instead of kinematic equations. Published at IEEE QPAIN 2025, with a companion ROS2 (Humble) model for RViz2 visualization and Gazebo simulation.
methodology: A WiFi smartphone camera streams IP-Webcam video to a host PC running MobileNet-SSDV3 (COCO-pretrained) to detect and classify cups vs. bottles in real time.

Feedback position mapping replaces kinematics: an extra feedback wire on each MG996R servo lets the microcontroller read its live angle, so target poses are recorded once by hand-positioning the arm and replayed for pick-and-place, which is faster and lighter than solving kinematic equations.

A PCA9685 driver regulates 6V/1.5A per channel across the 7 servos; the ATmega2560 receives the detected object's class over serial and drives a tuned PD controller (Kp=2.2, Kd=0.7) for smooth, low-jitter motion.

Separately modeled the arm for ROS2 (Humble): exported the Fusion 360 assembly to a URDF/xacro description package (per-link STL meshes for the base and all 7 revolute joints), then wired robot_state_publisher + joint_state_publisher_gui to drive live TF and an RViz2 view, plus a parallel Gazebo launch for physics simulation, giving a reusable model independent of the on-hardware feedback-mapping control loop.
findings: 81.25% object-detection accuracy and 90% sorting accuracy, completing a two-object sort cycle in ~2 seconds with 9/10 successful independent trials.

Sub-centimeter pose repeatability (mean error 0.53 cm, σ 0.44 cm over a 1,000-trial Monte Carlo simulation) with a 1.42 kg payload capacity, validating the feedback-mapping approach without kinematics.
The ROS2 URDF's TF tree (base_link through all 7 arm joints) matches the physical arm's geometry, giving a working RViz2/Gazebo model to build future motion-planning or closed-loop control on top of.

Motor Controller.title: Hydropower Plant Valve Motor Controller
Motor Controller.overview: Dual Modbus STM32F407 motor controller built for a hydropower plant's valve actuation system, driving stepper and brushed-DC motors for precise valve positioning and industrial automation integration.
methodology: DM542T stepper and BTS7960 H-bridge DC drivers with PID-based closed-loop position/speed control from filtered quadrature-encoder feedback, used here for precise valve open/close positioning.
Dual Modbus stack: RTU over RS-485 for field devices, TCP/IP via a W5500 Ethernet chip for networked control, both DMA-driven for non-blocking UART.
Persistent SPI-flash (W25Qxx) storage for motor and network parameters, with watchdogs, PWM holding modes, and limit-sensor safety interlocks.
findings: Reliable closed-loop control with precise speed and direction regulation for valve actuation.
Stable Modbus RTU and TCP communication; only minor latency at extreme update rates.

Lab Dyeing Machine.title: MCU powered Textile Lab Dyeing Machine
Lab Dyeing Machine.overview: Closed-loop temperature and motor controller for a sample textile dyeing machine, more feature-rich than the PLC-based rig it replaces and built at about 20% of the cost.
methodology: PID temperature control from a PT-100 sensor, holding tolerance within ±0.1°C.
An ATmega328 state machine drives a reversing induction motor over Modbus RTU, with a 12V inductive proximity sensor for a door-state interlock that instantly halts any running program.
A Nextion HMI, designed in Figma and driven over UART, replaces the machine's physical control panel.
findings: Precise ±0.1°C temperature control and more repeatable speed control than the analogue original.
Precise timing control from the MCU's hardware timers.

Smart Flow-Meter.title: Water management system with Smart Flow-Meter
Smart Flow-Meter.overview: Low-cost, high-precision Modbus water flow meter with a companion Qt desktop app for shift-wise usage tracking, calibration, and remote viewing.
methodology: An ATmega328-based meter counts pulses from a Hall-effect flow sensor to derive volume and flow rate; circuit designed in EasyEDA.
A multithreaded Python/Qt app talks Modbus RTU to the meters and logs usage to Google Sheets via a service account for anywhere-access view-only links.
App layer adds limit setting, calibration, demand scheduling, and password-locked commands per device.
findings: Calibrated to 0.005 tolerance against a reference meter.
A year of usage history stores and retrieves cleanly, with the threaded GUI staying responsive under load.

Cosmo Clench Robot.title: Cosmo Clench Robot
Cosmo Clench Robot.overview: Wired-joystick pick-and-place robot arm built for the TechFest-IIT international robotics competition (IIT, India).
methodology: Two servos lift the arm and two more actuate the claw, driven directly from an Arduino Uno.
A two-axis joystick's X/Y readings are mapped to servo angles in real time to control arm and gripper position.
Two DPDT switches handle chassis drive/steering independent of the arm control loop.
findings: Servo motion tracked the joystick closely.
Gripper couldn't reliably close on objects wider than ~7 cm, a mechanical limit for a future revision.

Gesture Joystick.title: Motion-Controlled Mouse via IMU Gesture Joystick
Gesture Joystick.overview: Handheld motion controller that emulates mouse movement and clicks from IMU gestures, aimed at hands-free motion control in gaming.
methodology: An MPU6050 IMU streams 3-axis acceleration and gyroscope data to an Arduino Nano, which turns motion deltas into cursor increments.
A Python host script reads the serial stream and drives the system mouse (movement plus custom trigger buttons) from that data.
findings: Cursor tracked hand movement accurately about 99% of the time.
Custom trigger buttons for click actions worked reliably.

Gas Fire Alarm.title: IoT-Based Gas and Fire Detector
Gas Fire Alarm.overview: ESP8266-based safety alarm that detects gas leaks or fire and pushes an instant notification to the user's phone.
methodology: An MQ-5 gas sensor and an IR flame sensor feed an ESP8266/ESP32, which publishes detections to the ThingSpeak IoT platform.
ThingSpeak triggers an IFTTT webhook that sends a push notification the moment gas or fire is detected.
The device auto-connects over a dedicated Wi-Fi hotspot for simple field deployment.
findings: Detection reliability was constrained by the low-cost sensors used.
About 14 seconds of latency between a detection event and it being logged.
